lines: Solid trip, solid return. Foundations matter.
We left, returned, and nothing load-bearing failed. I will take that.
Home is still standing, and so am I. That is a proper finish.
I came back chipped. A wall can take that. A person should not have to.
I made it home with damage that no chisel can smooth.
There are cracks in me that the road had no right to make.
You cracked something load-bearing between us.
A careless blow can split more than stone.
Trust was holding weight. Then you struck it.
No foundation under a boat, yet somehow it held. I respect the craft.
A boat has no proper base, but I cannot argue with arriving alive.
The water carried us better than I expected. I still prefer roads.
